item.title: ARMember WordPress Plugin Insecure Password Reset via Plaintext Key + SQLi Chain (CVE-2026-5076)

Summary

ARMember Premium <= 7.3.1 stores password-reset keys (arm_reset_password_key user meta) in plaintext, and the plugin’s member-directory AJAX endpoint (arm_directory_paging_action) is vulnerable to unauthenticated SQL injection via the order parameter. The included main.py exploit chains these together: it detects ARMember, locates a member-directory page to extract the required nonce/template ID, confirms boolean/time-based blind SQLi, enumerates the WordPress table prefix and admin account, triggers a password-reset request, and then uses the same blind SQLi to directly read the plaintext reset key (or the hashed WordPress user_activation_key as a fallback) out of the database. It then submits that key to either ARMember’s or WordPress’s own reset-password endpoint to set a new admin password and verifies login, achieving full administrator account takeover without ever needing to receive the reset email.
